commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36294: mempool: Remove -persistmempoolv1 option

731b89c09bbc286801eebf5061b161c3d5091150 test: Check that importmempool fails on a malformed mempool.dat (Fabian Jahr)
4c01625f798b4017ab83f86ab8815d56b4d18042 doc: Add release note for -persistmempoolv1 removal (Fabian Jahr)
d1dfdf827619bd06ff9c52e42f2c370e6e70504f mempool: Remove -persistmempoolv1 option (Fabian Jahr)
86a31b93d0db7f01e5c1a61fb014b89b2506fe54 test: Use v31.0 as old node in mempool_compatibility.py (Fabian Jahr)

Pull request description:

  `-persistmempoolv1` was added in #28207 as a temporary option to allow downgrading to v26 and earlier, which can't read the XOR'ed `mempool.dat`. v26 has now been EOL for a while. So any version this option could help downgrade to is unsupported now. It seems ready for removal. I don't think this requires an additional deprecation cycle since the feature is useless for any maintained version and docs have always stated that this was a "temporary option that will be removed in the future".

  Reading v1 files is still supported, so upgrading directly from an old version keeps the persisted mempool.

  `mempool_compatibility.py` now uses v28.2 as the old node, the oldest release in `get_previous_releases.py` that writes the current format.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36440: test: speed up functional tests by removing avoidable waits

8dc80cafa2ee5932c9ff499c02d6ab8e3cf2f5ef test: wake p2p wait_until on message delivery instead of polling (ViniciusCestarii)
10cfeb33357c937ddd9f588a35e0f8f33abd6ece test: set noban_tx_relay to speed up slow tx relay tests (ViniciusCestarii)

Pull request description:

  Reduce functional test runtime:

  - set noban_tx_relay = True for tests that can benefit from it.
  - wake P2PInterface.wait_until as soon as a message is delivered or the connection state changes, instead of polling every 50ms.

  Tested on my x86-64 machine:

  Wall time (-j=18): 110.8s to 99.1s (-11%)
  Accumulated: 1715s to 1411s (-17.5%)

  Tests that were most affected:

  | test | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | feature_maxuploadtarget | 57.9s | 6.2s |
  | wallet_conflicts | 49.2s | 7.0s |
  | p2p_sendheaders | 31.1s | 6.8s |
  | p2p_compactblocks | 11.1s | 1.7s |
  | wallet_orphanedreward | 9.3s | 5.2s |
  | wallet_importprunedfunds | 4.9s | 2.9s |

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#35989: wallet: fix crash on importdescriptors with a range ending at 2^31-1

93c8aec3fbc8c5a2fcc834c4acc1b7d96bffa9a0 doc: add release note for #35989 (Shuvam Pandey)
457c9e8999fbee1d37f41eaede681f787e657395 script: avoid overflow when checking descriptor range bounds (Shuvam Pandey)
ab3bb55a67cced3551e8ebb658c4d962a10d3715 test: add coverage for descriptor range end bounds (Shuvam Pandey)
867ad9bffbd3ab26c9899207ddd11380e0c1a1bd wallet: fix integer overflow in descriptor keypool top up (Shuvam Pandey)
1889440f821d6bf8394050c96cc8e06a2f18d9c2 wallet: reject unrepresentable descriptor import ranges (Shuvam Pandey)

Pull request description:

  `WalletDescriptor` stores an exclusive range end in `int32_t`. Importing
  `[2147483647, 2147483647]` produces an end of `2^31`, which narrows to a negative
  value and aborts the node during keypool top-up. An import without a range can
  hit the same issue with an oversized `-keypool`.

  Check the exclusive end before constructing the wallet descriptor, covering
  both explicit and default ranges. The bound stays wallet-specific: scanning
  RPCs still accept `INT32_MAX` as an inclusive endpoint.

  Also calculate the keypool top-up endpoint in `int64_t` before checking its
  bound, and reject reversed ranges before computing `high - low` in
  `CheckDescriptorRangeBounds`. These fix the overflows reached by
  `keypoolrefill INT32_MAX` after advancing a descriptor, and by `[INT64_MAX, 0]`,
  respectively. Regression tests cover all three fixes.

  I tested on macOS arm64 with Clang 22 and UBSan passed: 34 targeted unit
  cases and the importdescriptors, keypool, deriveaddresses (RPC and CLI),
  scantxoutset, and scanblocks functional tests.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36450: test: Use timeout_factor for drain timeout in check_slow_read_throttle

fa845f76d5c6d9c4aba46e03eb9b77a6e1f5ddce test: Use timeout_factor for drain timeout in check_slow_read_throttle (MarcoFalke)

Pull request description:

  The `check_slow_read_throttle` functional test may intermittently fail on slow build configs (like sanitizers+debug+no-opt). This is fine, but it would be nice if it passed.

  To reproduce the failure, add a long sleep for the big json requests:

  ```diff
  diff --git a/src/httpserver.cpp b/src/httpserver.cpp
  index 0c25ebbba5..42c54c2cdf 100644
  --- a/src/httpserver.cpp
  +++ b/src/httpserver.cpp
  @@ -614,2 +614,3 @@ void HTTPRemoteClient::Send(const HTTPResponse& res, std::span<const std::byte>
       bool send_buffer_was_empty{false};
  +    bool send_buffer_over_limit{false};
       // Fill the send buffer with the complete serialized response headers + body
  @@ -634,2 +635,4 @@ void HTTPRemoteClient::Send(const HTTPResponse& res, std::span<const std::byte>
           if (!send_buffer_was_empty) m_send_ready = true;
  +
  +        send_buffer_over_limit = m_send_buffer.size() > MAX_BODY_SIZE;
       }
  @@ -652,2 +655,11 @@ void HTTPRemoteClient::Send(const HTTPResponse& res, std::span<const std::byte>

  +    // TEST-ONLY: Widen the interval between queueing a throttling-sized response
  +    // and allowing the next pipelined request to be dispatched. This reproduces
  +    // the slow-worker scheduling window exercised by interface_http.py.
  +    if (send_buffer_over_limit) {
  +    // The functional test waits twice for five seconds before it starts
  +    // its own ten-second recv() timeout, so this must cover both phases.
  +    std::this_thread::sleep_for(30s);
  +    }
  +
       // Signal to the I/O loop that we are ready to handle the next request.
  ```

  Then, on master (or on this pull with `--timeout-factor=1`), it will fail and with `--timeout-factor=3` it will pass:

  ```
  ./bld-cmake/test/functional/interface_http.py --test_methods check_slow_read_throttle --loglevel=DEBUG --timeout-factor 3
  ```

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#34374: kernel: use struct-based logging and simplify logging interface

eb086540b680cfed42ab7f9498c1ade459828808 kernel: make logging struct-based and simplify configuration (stickies-v)
0c327a34748a3d882d88fe0034187ddee0c7d59a kernel: add KernelLogger (stickies-v)
3d976f464d5a5dbb0b867783c472b31ba871900a kernel: remove API to format and disable logging (stickies-v)

Pull request description:

  tl;dr: kernel logging is cumbersome. This PR delivers log entries as a struct instead of a formatted string, and simplifies the kernel logging interface. Closes #34062.

  ## Motivation

  The `bitcoinkernel` library (#27587) [exposes](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/b26762bdcb941096ccc6f53c3fb5a7786ad735e7/src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.h#L698-L778) functionality to interface with the kernel logging. This includes registering callbacks for log statements, level/category filtering, string formatting options, and more.

  Kernel logging has a few problems:
  - [callbacks](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/b26762bdcb941096ccc6f53c3fb5a7786ad735e7/src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.h#L304) operate on formatted strings, so users need to parse the string to get the timestamp, category, level, ... based on which options are set. This is cumbersome, brittle, and inefficient.
  - the [filtering interface](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/b26762bdcb941096ccc6f53c3fb5a7786ad735e7/src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.h#L737) is not really intuitive, requiring users to call combinations of `btck_logging_set_level_category` and `btck_logging_enable_category` when they want to produce `debug` or `trace` logs. The level/category system makes sense for node, because it directly controls what gets written to disk and stdout, and there are quite a lot more categories producing logs. Kernel doesn't really need this - users control what happens to the logs, and can do any filtering/manipulation in the callback they provide.
  - the node logging infrastructure has quite a bit more functionality than is necessary for a library, including ratelimiting, log formatting, outputting, buffering, ... This introduces unnecessary code and interface complexity.

  ## Approach

  Log generation (`util/log.h`: macros, `util::log::Entry`, and the `ShouldDebugLog`/`ShouldTraceLog`/`Log` hooks an application must provide) was already separated from log handling (`logging.h`) in #34465 and subsequent PRs.   2. **Add `KernelLogger`**: a kernel-owned backend that holds the registered callbacks and the minimum level, and converts each `util::log::Entry` into a `btck_LogEntry`. Introduced in a separate commit to keep the scope of the behaviour-changing commit smaller.

  - Logging callbacks deliver structs instead of formatted strings, and the entire logging interface is simplified.

  - Messages are delivered unescaped and without a trailing newline.

  ### `bitcoinkernel` C logging interface

  ```c

      const char* message;    //! Log message text.
      size_t message_len;
      const char* thread_name;    //! Name of the thread that produced the log message.
      size_t thread_name_len;
      int64_t timestamp_ns;    //! Wall-clock time when the entry was logged, in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch.
      int64_t mocktime_s;    //! Mock time in effect when the entry was logged, in seconds since the Unix epoch, or 0 if no mock time is set (see btck_set_mock_time).
      const char* file_name;    //! Name of the source file that produced the log statement.
      size_t file_name_len;
      const char* function_name;    //! Name of the function that produced the log message.
      size_t function_name_len;
      uint32_t line;    //! Line number of the source code that produced the log statement.
      btck_LogLevel level;    //! Log severity level.
      btck_LogCategory category;    //! Log category.
  } btck_LogEntry;

  BITCOINKERNEL_API void btck_logging_set_min_level(btck_LogLevel level);

  BITCOINKERNEL_API btck_LoggingConnection* BITCOINKERNEL_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT btck_logging_connection_create(
      btck_LogCallback log_callback,
      void* user_data,
      btck_DestroyCallback user_data_destroy_callback) BITCOINKERNEL_ARG_NONNULL(1);

  BITCOINKERNEL_API void btck_logging_connection_destroy(btck_LoggingConnection* logging_connection);
  ```
